t: Number of Nodes With Value One
o: The tree is the implicit complete-binary-tree labeling: parent of v is v//2, root 1. Each query flips every node in the subtree of the queried label. After all flips we count nodes holding 1. A node ends as 1 iff it was flipped an odd number of times, i.e., iff its ancestor-or-self query labels were issued an odd number of times overall. In example 1 (n=5, queries [1,2,5]): node 1 flipped once (query 1) plus once via query 2 → twice → 0? The expected answer counts nodes 1,3,5 — node 1 receives flips from queries 1 and 2 (even → 0)? Recomputing: query 1 flips {1,2,3,4,5}, query 2 flips {2,4,5}, query 5 flips {5}. Node 1: one flip → 1. Node 2: two → 0. Node 3: one → 1. Node 4: two → 0. Node 5: three → 1. Total 3, matching. So per node we just need the parity of flips on its root-path. Equivalently, for each query node q issued c times with c odd, all size(q) nodes in its subtree toggle — but overlapping toggles mean we cannot simply sum sizes; instead compute, for each node, the parity along its path, or aggregate: a node v is 1 iff the number of queried ancestors (inclusive) with odd multiplicity on its path is odd. The clean implementation: count multiplicities of query labels; for each node v, walk up to the root summing parities — O(n log n) worst case, or better: propagate parity downward from each oddly-queried node over its subtree with a shared toggle array via DFS on the implicit tree.
k: A node is finally 1 iff an odd number of queried ancestors-or-self had odd query multiplicity.
Subtree of v in this implicit tree is just v, 2v, 2v+1, 4v, … truncated at n — enumerable without building the tree.

a.n: Approach 1: Parity propagation over implicit subtrees
a.i: Count how often each label is queried. For each label with odd count, XOR-flip a state bit for every node in its implicit subtree (enumerate v, 2v, 2v+1, … ≤ n via a stack). Finally sum the state array. Complexity is bounded by the total subtree sizes, at most O(Q · n) worst case but typically far less; a cleaner bound comes from doing it level-synchronously, still simple and passes given Q, n ≤ 1e5 with early truncation.
s: For each label with odd count, traverse its implicit subtree (stack of descendants ≤ n) toggling state[v].
a.t: O(Q·depth + n) in typical cases; worst case O(n·Q) but fast in practice due to subtree truncation at n

a.i: Directly apply the characterization: node v ends as 1 iff the number of ancestors-or-self of v whose query count is odd, is odd. Walk each v up by v //= 2, summing odd-multiplicity flags. O(n log n) time, O(1) extra beyond the count map.
s: For each v from 1 to n, climb parent pointers accumulating odd-count flags.
Answer = number of v with odd accumulated flag.
a.t: O(n log n + Q) — each node climbs log n parents

w: Approach 1 is the standard editorial solution; approach 2 is a nice alternative showing the parity characterization. Duplicate queries matter — only parity of each label's count influences the result. Verify with example 2 (queries [2,3,3]: label 3 cancels, only subtree of 2 toggles → node 2 is 1, answer 1). Follow-up: stream queries with online answers — you would maintain subtree-toggle counts with a BIT over Euler tours of the implicit tree.
